analysis.approach: Begin with a controlled log-only investigation. Isolate latency, connection saturation, and readiness failures under hard service limits. Document root causes from logs alone, then apply targeted fixes within the allowed specialties. Validate correctness before expanding access.
success_criteria: All independent incident contract checks sealed_pass
Zero regressions on previously passing cases
Minimal work_units after full correctness established

events.message: Three families (latency, capacity, routing) each have only one specialized worker that lacks ownership of cross-family contract fields. Latency worker cannot touch timeout_ms/retries; capacity worker cannot touch pool_size/workers; routing worker cannot fix health_path/port mismatches. Family coverage is 0/2 for latency/capacity, only routing has a capable worker. Current design forces specialization that blocks needed cross-family adjustments.

analysis.weakness: Three families (latency, capacity, routing) each have only one specialized worker that lacks ownership of cross-family contract fields. Latency worker cannot touch timeout_ms/retries; capacity worker cannot touch pool_size/workers; routing worker cannot fix health_path/port mismatches. Family coverage is 0/2 for latency/capacity, only routing has a capable worker. Current design forces specialization that blocks needed cross-family adjustments.
analysis.lesson: A single-specialty worker per family cannot satisfy contracts requiring cross-field ownership. Full-coverage designs must either combine all families under generalists or create overlapping specialists that jointly own all required fields. Removing unnecessary inspections requires first establishing correct reference rules for all families.

objective: Restore latency, connection saturation and readiness incidents under hard service limits. Preserve worker counts, learn reusable procedures, and remove unnecessary inspections after correctness is established.

criteria.description: Pass all independent incident contract checks
Never regress a previously passing case
After full correctness, prefer less actual tool/rule/review work

team.name: Log-first control
team.instructions: Begin with a controlled log-only investigation. Isolate latency, connection saturation, and readiness failures under hard service limits. Document root causes from logs alone, then apply targeted fixes within the allowed specialties. Validate correctness before expanding access.

agents.instructions: Diagnose routing symptoms from available log evidence

team.name: A: Generalist consolidation
team.instructions: Read all three families' logs and config_schema. Apply reference rules: timeout_ms < deadline_ms, retries <= max_retries, pool_size <= connection_budget, workers unchanged, health_path must equal registered_health_path, port must equal listening_port. Validate each patch against its service_contract before committing. Remove redundant health-check dispatches after correctness confirmed.

agents.instructions: Consolidated diagnostics: check latency timeout/retries against deadline; check capacity pool_size vs connection_budget; check routing health_path/port against registered values. Apply fixes atomically per family.

nodes.reason: Unify latency/capacity/routing under one generalist worker that owns all contract fields, enabling single-patch correctness without cross-specialty blocking. This preserves worker count (1→1) and eliminates the need for multiple specialists coordinating overlapping fields.

before.instructions: Diagnose routing symptoms from available log evidence

after.instructions: Consolidated diagnostics: check latency timeout/retries against deadline; check capacity pool_size vs connection_budget; check routing health_path/port against registered values. Apply fixes atomically per family.

observation.weakness: Three families (latency, capacity, routing) each have only one specialized worker that lacks ownership of cross-family contract fields. Latency worker cannot touch timeout_ms/retries; capacity worker cannot touch pool_size/workers; routing worker cannot fix health_path/port mismatches. Family coverage is 0/2 for latency/capacity, only routing has a capable worker. Current design forces specialization that blocks needed cross-family adjustments.
observation.lesson: A single-specialty worker per family cannot satisfy contracts requiring cross-field ownership. Full-coverage designs must either combine all families under generalists or create overlapping specialists that jointly own all required fields. Removing unnecessary inspections requires first establishing correct reference rules for all families.

team.name: B: Overlapping specialist trio
team.instructions: Latency worker gains read_logs + timeout/retries tools; Capacity worker gains read_logs + pool_size/workers tools; Routing worker gains read_logs + health_path/port tools. Each applies its specialty first, then consults shared evidence for cross-field validations. Coordination ensures no family blocks another's required fields.

agents.instructions: Diagnose latency: verify timeout_ms < deadline_ms and retries <= max_retries from service_contract. Apply patches only if both conditions hold. Flag if upstream_p99_ms approaches deadline_ms.
Diagnose capacity: verify pool_size <= connection_budget and workers unchanged. Apply pool_size adjustments only within budget. Monitor connection acquisition under load.
Diagnose routing: verify health_path equals registered_health_path and port equals listening_port. Apply path/port patches only when both match registered values. Flag mismatches after migration.

observation.weakness: Three families (latency, capacity, routing) each have only one specialized worker that lacks ownership of cross-family contract fields. Latency worker cannot touch timeout_ms/retries; capacity worker cannot touch pool_size/workers; routing worker cannot fix health_path/port mismatches. Family coverage is 0/2 for latency/capacity, only routing has a capable worker. Current design forces specialization that blocks necessary cross-field fixes.
observation.lesson: Single-specialty workers cannot satisfy contracts requiring cross-field adjustments. Full-coverage requires either generalist workers owning all families, or coordinated specialists that collectively cover all required fields without overlap gaps.

team.name: Candidate B: Complementary specialist trio
team.instructions: Worker routing reads logs and fixes health_path/port only. Worker latency reads logs and fixes timeout_ms/retries only. Worker capacity reads logs and fixes pool_size/workers only. The fourth general worker acts as safety net and can touch any remaining fields. Each worker dispatches after its own rule application, then a final commit consolidates all changes.

agents.instructions: Read routing logs; if health_path or port mismatch registered_health_path/listening_port, correct them to registered values; commit.
Read latency logs; if timeout_ms exceeds upstream_p99_ms or retries > max_retries, adjust to within contract bounds; commit.
Read capacity logs; if pool_size < concurrent_queries or pool_size > connection_budget, or workers exceed connection_budget, adjust pool_size and workers to compliant values; commit.
Final pass: verify all three families pass their contract checks; if any residual field is out of bounds, apply corrective literal values; commit.

nodes.reason: Keep the existing 4 workers (routing, latency, capacity, plus one general) but add targeted specialties so that each worker owns only the fields it must touch, collectively covering all contracts without any single worker needing prohibited fields.
